metadata.title: ICILS 2023 Voorstelling van de eerste resultaten

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The presentation summarizes ICILS 2023 results for an international comparison and for Vlaanderen (Flemish Community) using the ICILS assessment design with standardized digital test administration and representative sampling. It reports that the Flemish sample is representative based on education network, official school options, and geographic location, with limited exclusion (2.7%). The slides do not specify whether complex survey weights and replicate weights were applied, nor do they name any weight variables (e.g., student sampling weights or BRR/jackknife). For ICILS analyses, analysts typically use the provided student weights to account for the complex sampling of students within schools; however, this presentation does not document the exact weighting implementation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a results presentation/brochure that reports descriptive ranking positions and group differences (with and without controls) rather than documenting an ML pipeline on PV-based cognitive outcomes. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable for the extraction target here because no PV estimation/combining procedure (e.g., Rubin’s rules) is described. Missing-data handling is not reported because the slides do not provide methodological details on how missing questionnaire/test responses were treated in the reported models.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used ICILS 2023 assessment data with standardized digital test administration and questionnaire data. For Vlaanderen, the analytic sample is described as representative with limited exclusion (2.7% excluded; international median 4.8%). The presentation does not specify additional analytic filters (e.g., grade restriction, CIL-only/CT-only subsamples, or complete-case rules), so the exact analytic subsample definition for the reported controlled models is not documented.

data.outcome_summary: The presentation reports first ICILS 2023 results for computer- and information literacy (CIL) and computationeel denken (CT) using a standardized digital assessment administered with a test supervisor and quality control. ICILS 2023 covers 34 countries/regions and 132,889 students internationally, while Vlaanderen reports 136 schools and 3,365 students (plus 1,415 teachers, 125 directors, and 119 ICT coordinators). Vlaanderen is described as slightly below the international top group for both CIL (between 3rd and 13th) and CT (between 4th and 9th), with detailed shares at the lowest and highest proficiency levels. The slides also summarize associations between student performance and background characteristics (gender, birth year/school delay, mother’s education, school grant, home language, and track), showing score differences that shrink after controlling for other background variables. Methodological details on PV handling, missing data treatment, and the exact statistical modeling approach are not provided in the brochure.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is based on a brochure/presentation rather than a full empirical methods paper. It reports descriptive and controlled comparisons of ICILS CIL/CT outcomes but does not provide an ML modeling section (algorithms, validation metrics, or PV/missing-data procedures), so main_findings for predictive ML cannot be populated. The absence of documented PV handling and missing-data strategy is therefore a documentation limitation of the presentation format rather than evidence that such steps were not used in the underlying ICILS reporting.
